messages:
alex: Heads-up — hit a confusing error mapping in Python SDK: sometimes we get a 200 with an error body and end up raising GenericSDKError. Customers can't distinguish auth vs quota. Thoughts?
mira: Seen that before. Does the response ever include an x-rw-error-code or similar header?
alex: sometimes. Example body: {"error": {"type": "rate_limit", "msg": "Too many requests"}} but HTTP status is 200.
sam: That's the core issue — our clients treat HTTP status as source of truth. We should define precedence: header -> body -> status, and document it.
lindsey: Also propose returning typed exceptions across SDKs: AuthError, RateLimitError, BadRequestError, ServiceUnavailableError, and a RetryableError base for transient ones.
mira: Agree but avoid leaking internal IDs in top-line messages. Keep a friendly human message and expose a machine-readable code property for programmatic use.
alex: Draft mapping: if x-rw-error-code header present -> map to typed exc; else if body.error.type present -> map to typed exc; else map from HTTP status code. Crucial: if status is 200 but body indicates error, treat as error not success.
sam: Also for retries: SDKs should surface should_retry boolean + retry_after when available, and built-in retryers should respect those.
mira: Can we add a helper like Response.to_error() returning a typed error object with fields: code, category, retryable, hint? Example snippet: 
```
err = resp.to_error()
if isinstance(err, RateLimitError) and err.retry_after:
    sleep(err.retry_after)
```
That keeps app code ergonomic.
alex: UX copy guidance: avoid raw stack traces or internal ids in user-facing messages. Use: "Request blocked: rate limit" and include useful meta in error.code/metadata and a suggested action (e.g., "retry after Xs or reduce concurrency").
lindsey: Initial status mapping table idea: 429 -> RateLimitError (retryable true), 401/403 -> AuthError (retryable false), 400 -> BadRequestError (retryable false), 5xx -> ServiceUnavailableError (retryable true). Special case: 200 + body.error.type -> map according to body.type.
mira: Need parity across languages. Right now JS favors body-first, Py favors status-first. We should ship a canonical spec + conformance tests.
dev-bot: Created INF-2345: "error mapping spec" and linked draft PR #4567.
alex: I'll draft the spec + python PR and add a quickstart snippet showing typed error handling. Anyone pair on JS parity tomorrow? @sam
sam: I'll join 10am PT. Also propose a tiny sample app branch demonstrating best-practice handling + retry helpers for onboarding. :thumbsup:
